title.raw: 《列傳‧伯夷列傳》 Biographies - Biography of Bo Yi

sentences.zh: 夫學者載籍極博，猶考信於六藝。

translations.literal: Scholars' recorded writings are exceedingly vast, yet they still verify trustworthiness against the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The writings preserved by scholars are exceedingly vast, yet they still verify their trustworthiness against the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 詩書雖缺，然虞夏之文可知也。

translations.literal: Though the Poetry and Documents are incomplete, yet the writings of Yu and Xia can still be known.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Poetry and Documents are incomplete, the writings of Yu and Xia can still be known.

sentences.zh: 堯將遜位，讓於虞舜，舜禹之閒，岳牧咸薦，乃試之於位，典職數十年，功用既興，然後授政。

translations.literal: Yao was about to abdicate the throne and yield it to Yu Shun; between Shun and Yu, the mountain lords and pastors all recommended him; then they tested him in office, he held his duties for several decades, and when his merits and achievements had flourished, they transferred the administration to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao was about to abdicate the throne and yield it to Yu Shun, the mountain lords and pastors all recommended him. They tested him in office; he held his duties for several decades, and when his merits and achievements had flourished, they transferred the administration to him.

sentences.zh: 示天下重器，王者大統，傳天下若斯之難也。

translations.literal: Thus, showing the world the great vessel of state and the king's supreme succession—transmitting the realm is so difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, they showed the world the great vessel of state and the king's supreme succession—transmitting the realm is so difficult.

sentences.zh: 而說者曰堯讓天下於許由，許由不受，恥之逃隱。

translations.literal: Yet storytellers say Yao yielded the realm to Xu You; Xu You did not accept, took it as shame, and fled into seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet storytellers say that Yao yielded the realm to Xu You, that Xu You did not accept, and that, ashamed, he fled into seclusion.

sentences.zh: 及夏之時，有卞隨、務光者。

translations.literal: And in Xia's time, there were Bian Sui and Wu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: And in Xia's time, there were Bian Sui and Wu Guang.

sentences.zh: 此何以稱焉？

translations.literal: How is this to be regarded?
translations.idiomatic: How is this to be regarded?

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：余登箕山，其上蓋有許由冢云。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: I ascended Mount Ji, and on it there is said to be the tomb of Xu You.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: I ascended Mount Ji, and on it there is said to be the tomb of Xu You.

sentences.zh: 孔子序列古之仁聖賢人，如吳太伯、伯夷之倫詳矣。

translations.literal: Confucius set forth the ancient benevolent sages and worthy men, such as Wu Taibo and Bo Yi, in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius set forth the ancient benevolent sages and worthy men, such as Wu Taibo and Bo Yi, in detail.

sentences.zh: 余以所聞由、光義至高，其文辭不少概見，何哉？

translations.literal: As for the righteousness of Xu You and Wu Guang, of which I have heard, it is extremely lofty; yet their accounts are not visible even in the slightest overview—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: The righteousness of men such as Xu You and Wu Guang, of which I have heard, is very lofty indeed; yet one cannot find even the slightest trace of them in the writings of the past—why is this?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「伯夷、叔齊，不念舊惡，怨是用希。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Bo Yi and Shu Qi do not remember old wrongs; therefore resentment toward them is rare.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Bo Yi and Shu Qi do not remember old wrongs; therefore resentment toward them is rare."

sentences.zh: 「求仁得仁，又何怨乎？」

translations.literal: 'They sought benevolence and obtained benevolence—what resentment then?'
translations.idiomatic: "They sought benevolence and obtained benevolence—what resentment then?"

sentences.zh: 余悲伯夷之意，睹軼詩可異焉。

translations.literal: I grieve for Bo Yi's intent; seeing the lost poem, one finds it strange indeed.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for Bo Yi's intent; when one sees the lost poem, it is strange indeed.

sentences.zh: 其傳曰：

translations.literal: The biography says:
translations.idiomatic: The biography says:

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊，孤竹君之二子也。

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were the two sons of the lord of Guzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were the two sons of the lord of Guzhu.

sentences.zh: 父欲立叔齊，及父卒，叔齊讓伯夷。

translations.literal: Father wished to establish Shu Qi, when father died, Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Their father wished to establish Shu Qi. When their father died, Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.

sentences.zh: 伯夷曰：「父命也。」

translations.literal: Bo Yi said: 'It is our father's command.'
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi said, "It is our father's command."

sentences.zh: 遂逃去。

translations.literal: Thus, fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, he fled away.

sentences.zh: 叔齊亦不肯立而逃之。

translations.literal: Shu Qi also refused to take the throne and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Qi also refused to take the throne and fled.

sentences.zh: 國人立其中子。

translations.literal: The people of the state established their middle son.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the state established their middle son.

sentences.zh: 於是伯夷、叔齊聞西伯昌善養老，盍往歸焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bo Yi and Shu Qi heard that the Earl of the West, Chang, was good at supporting the elderly, and thought, why not go and attach themselves to him?
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Bo Yi and Shu Qi heard that the Earl of the West, Chang, was good at supporting the elderly, and thought they would go and attach themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 及至，西伯卒，武王載木主，號為文王，東伐紂。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Earl of the West had died; King Wu carried the wooden spirit tablet, styled him King Wen, and marched east to attack King Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the Earl of the West had died. King Wu carried the wooden spirit tablet, styled him King Wen, and marched east to attack King Zhou.

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊叩馬而諫曰：「父死不葬，爰及干戈，可謂孝乎？

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi grasped the horse and remonstrated saying: 'Father died not buried, moreover to weapons, can this be called filial?
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi grasped the horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying: 'Father has died and not been buried, yet you resort to weapons—can this be called filial?

sentences.zh: 以臣弒君，可謂仁乎？」

translations.literal: With minister killing lord, can this be called benevolent?'
translations.idiomatic: For a minister to kill his lord—can this be called benevolent?'

sentences.zh: 左右欲兵之。

translations.literal: Those at his side wished to use weapons on them.
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side wished to kill them with weapons.

sentences.zh: 太公曰：「此義人也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said: 'These are righteous men.'
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke said: 'These are righteous men.'

sentences.zh: 扶而去之。

translations.literal: Supported and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He supported them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 武王已平殷亂，天下宗周，而伯夷、叔齊恥之，義不食周粟，隱於首陽山，采薇而食之。

translations.literal: King Wu having pacified the Yin disorder, the world took Zhou as its lord, yet Bo Yi and Shu Qi were ashamed of this; for righteousness they would not eat Zhou grain; they hid on Mount Shouyang, gathered ferns, and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu had pacified the disorder of Yin and the world acknowledged Zhou as paramount, Bo Yi and Shu Qi were ashamed of it. For righteousness' sake they would not eat Zhou grain. They hid on Mount Shouyang, gathered ferns, and ate them.

sentences.zh: 及餓且死，作歌。

translations.literal: When hungry and about to die, composed a song.
translations.idiomatic: When they were hungry and about to die, they composed a song.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：「登彼西山兮，采其薇矣。

translations.literal: The lyrics say: 'Ascending that western mountain, gathering its ferns.
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics say: 'Ascending that western mountain, gathering its ferns.

sentences.zh: 以暴易暴兮，不知其非矣。

translations.literal: Replacing violence with violence—we do not know its wrongness.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing violence with violence—we do not know its wrongness.

sentences.zh: 神農、虞、夏忽焉沒兮，我安適歸矣？

translations.literal: Shennong, Yu, Xia suddenly gone, where shall I return?
translations.idiomatic: Shennong, Yu, and Xia have suddenly perished—where shall I return?

sentences.zh: 于嗟徂兮，命之衰矣！」

translations.literal: Alas going, fate's decline!'
translations.idiomatic: Alas, I am going—fate's decline!'

sentences.zh: 遂餓死於首陽山。

translations.literal: Thus, they starved to death on Mount Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, they starved to death on Mount Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，怨邪非邪？

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, was there resentment or not?
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in this light, was there resentment or not?

sentences.zh: 或曰：「天道無親，常與善人。」

translations.literal: Some say: 'Heaven's way has no partiality, constantly with good people.'
translations.idiomatic: Some say: 'Heaven's way has no partiality—it constantly sides with good people.'

sentences.zh: 若伯夷、叔齊，可謂善人者非邪？

translations.literal: As for Bo Yi and Shu Qi—were they not good men?
translations.idiomatic: As for Bo Yi and Shu Qi—were they not good men?

sentences.zh: 積仁絜行如此而餓死！

translations.literal: Accumulated benevolence and pure conduct like this yet starved to death!
translations.idiomatic: They accumulated benevolence and pure conduct like this, yet starved to death!

sentences.zh: 且七十子之徒，仲尼獨薦顏淵為好學。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the seventy disciples, Confucius alone praised Yan Yuan as fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the seventy disciples, Confucius alone praised Yan Yuan as fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 然回也屢空，糟糠不厭，而卒蚤夭。

translations.literal: Yet Yan Hui often was empty, did not reject coarse food, yet died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan Hui often went hungry, did not reject coarse food, and ultimately died young.

sentences.zh: 天之報施善人，其何如哉？

translations.literal: Heaven's reward and punishment for good people, what is it like?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's rewards and punishments for good people—what are they like?

sentences.zh: 盜蹠日殺不辜，肝人之肉，暴戾恣睢，聚黨數千人橫行天下，竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent and ate human flesh; violent and arrogant, he gathered a band of several thousand men and rampaged across the realm, yet in the end died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent and ate human flesh. Violent and arrogant, he gathered a band of several thousand men and rampaged across the realm, yet in the end died of old age.

sentences.zh: 是遵何德哉？

translations.literal: This followed what virtue?
translations.idiomatic: What virtue did this follow?

sentences.zh: 此其尤大彰明較著者也。

translations.literal: This is the most glaringly clear and evident example.
translations.idiomatic: This is the most glaringly clear and evident example.

sentences.zh: 若至近世，操行不軌，專犯忌諱，而終身逸樂，富厚累世不絕。

translations.literal: If we come to recent times, those whose conduct is unseemly and who deliberately violate taboos yet enjoy ease and pleasure all their lives, with wealth and eminence continuing for generations without end—
translations.idiomatic: If we come to recent times, there are those whose conduct is unseemly and who deliberately violate taboos, yet enjoy ease and pleasure all their lives, with wealth and eminence continuing for generations without end.

sentences.zh: 或擇地而蹈之，時然後出言，行不由徑，非公正不發憤，而遇禍災者，不可勝數也。

translations.literal: Others tread only on proper ground, speak only when the time is right, walk by no crooked path, and vent indignation only when faced with injustice—yet those who meet with disaster are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Others tread only on proper ground, speak only when the time is right, walk by no crooked path, and vent indignation only when faced with injustice—yet those who meet with disaster are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 余甚惑焉，儻所謂天道，是邪非邪？

translations.literal: I am greatly confused about this, perhaps what is called heaven's way, is it so or not?
translations.idiomatic: I am greatly confused about this. Perhaps what is called heaven's way—is it so or not?

sentences.zh: 子曰「道不同不相為謀」，亦各從其志也。

translations.literal: The Master said, 'Those whose ways differ do not take counsel together'—each follows his own aim.
translations.idiomatic: The Master said, "Those whose ways differ do not take counsel together"—each follows his own aim.

sentences.zh: 故曰「富貴如可求，雖執鞭之士，吾亦為之。

translations.literal: Therefore, it is said, 'If wealth and nobility can be sought, even as one who holds the whip I would do it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, it is said, "If wealth and nobility can be sought, even as one who holds the whip I would do it.

sentences.zh: 如不可求，從吾所好」。

translations.literal: If they cannot be sought, I will follow what I love.'
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot be sought, I will follow what I love."

sentences.zh: 「歲寒，然後知松柏之後凋」。

translations.literal: 'Year's cold, then know pine and cypress wither late.'
translations.idiomatic: 'In the year's cold, then know the pine and cypress wither late.'

sentences.zh: 舉世混濁，清士乃見。

translations.literal: When the whole world is murky and confused, the pure gentleman then appears.
translations.idiomatic: When the whole world is murky and confused, the pure gentleman then appears.

sentences.zh: 豈以其重若彼，其輕若此哉？

translations.literal: Is it because what is weighty is as that, and what is light is as this?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because what is weighty counts for that, and what is light counts for this?

sentences.zh: 「君子疾沒世而名不稱焉。」

translations.literal: 'The gentleman hates to leave the world with his name unpraised.'
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman hates to leave the world with his name unpraised.

sentences.zh: 賈子曰：「貪夫徇財，烈士徇名，夸者死權，眾庶馮生。」

translations.literal: Master Jia said: 'The greedy man dies for wealth, the ardent knight dies for fame, the boaster dies for power, the common multitude cling to life.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Jia said, "The greedy man dies for wealth, the ardent knight dies for fame, the boaster dies for power, the common multitude cling to life."

sentences.zh: 「同明相照，同類相求。」

translations.literal: 'Like brightness illuminates one another; like kind seeks one another.'
translations.idiomatic: "Like brightness illuminates one another; like kind seeks one another."

sentences.zh: 雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物睹。」

translations.literal: 'Clouds follow the dragon, wind follows the tiger; when a sage arises, the myriad things look to him.'
translations.idiomatic: "Clouds follow the dragon, wind follows the tiger; when a sage arises, the myriad things look to him."

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊雖賢，得夫子而名益彰。

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi, though worthy, came to have the Master, and their names became the more illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were worthy men, but once they had the Master, their names became all the more illustrious.

sentences.zh: 顏淵雖篤學，附驥尾而行益顯。

translations.literal: Yan Yuan, though he studied with utmost devotion, by attaching to a steed's tail his conduct became the more prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yuan studied with utmost devotion; by attaching himself to a great steed's tail, his conduct became all the more prominent.

sentences.zh: 巖穴之士，趣舍有時若此，類名堙滅而不稱，悲夫！

translations.literal: Recluses of cliff and cave, advancing and withdrawing as the times require—like these, whole classes of names are buried in oblivion and go unmentioned. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Recluses of cliff and cave, advancing and withdrawing as the times require—like these, whole classes of names are buried in oblivion and go unmentioned. Alas!

sentences.zh: 閭巷之人，欲砥行立名者，非附青雲之士，惡能施于後世哉？

translations.literal: Men of lanes and alleys who wish to polish their conduct and establish their names—if they do not attach themselves to men who have risen to the blue clouds, how can they leave their mark on posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Men of lanes and alleys who wish to polish their conduct and establish their names—if they do not attach themselves to men who have risen to the blue clouds, how can they leave their mark on posterity?
